subject: SLA: uptime threshold & monthly credit cap — Skyforge negotiation
messages:
From: Claire Morton <claire@skyforge.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Lee <tim.lee@skyforge.ai>, procurement@skyforge.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: SLA request: 99.95 uptime + monthly credit cap adjustment

Aditya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited about Redwood for inference, but Procurement has pushed back on the standard SLA draft. Two asks from our side to get this over the line:

1) Uptime floor: we need a 99.95% monthly uptime commitment (not the 99.9% in your template). Our app is customer-facing and even short degradations materially impact revenue.

2) Monthly credit cap: the template caps remedy at 30% of monthly invoice. Given potential business impact, we need a higher short-term cap (propose 60% during ramp) and a path to reduce once we're past the pilot.

We understand you have operational constraints — happy to accept carveouts for planned maintenance and a short latency SLO exception for batched inference during known ramp windows — but we need the availability floor and the monthly credit economics revised for procurement approval.

I've attached the SOW with our redlines. Procurement timeline is tight — we need terms agreed by EOD Monday (7/19) to make the quarter plan. Can your team run numbers and propose a compromise?

Claire Morton
Director of Platform Ops
Skyforge AI
(Attachment: Skyforge_SOW_SLA_redlines.pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Claire Morton <claire@skyforge.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA request: 99.95 uptime + monthly credit cap adjustment

Claire —

Appreciate the clear asks and the SOW redlines. Looping in Laura (Commercial) and Marissa (Legal/Customer Success) to help surface options. We reviewed your requests and proposed a few pragmatic approaches so we can move quickly: 

Option A (Pilot compromise):
- 99.95% uptime for an initial 6-month pilot period.
- Monthly credit formula: breaches pay up to 60% of the monthly invoice during the pilot, limited to a max of 2x the per-incident remedy multiplier (to avoid runaway exposure).
- We retain standard maintenance carveouts (48-hour notice for non-emergency maintenance; emergency maintenance subject to post-incident review).

Option B (Standard + higher cap for severe outages):
- Standard platform SLA of 99.9% long-term.
- Monthly cap increases only for defined severity incidents: a single critical outage (>=6 hours) triggers an elevated cap up to 60% that month; otherwise standard 30% cap applies.

Operational notes: we can provide P95 latency targets for your primary endpoints (we'll need your traffic/sequence-length profile to set realistic numbers for batched inference). For billing/crediting we can run an expected exposure model if you share estimated monthly spend and peak traffic windows.

Attached: our working SLA template (redwood_sla_template_v2.pdf) with tracked edits showing the above options. Asking Laura and Marissa to confirm legal/financial guardrails and whether we can bind Option A as a pilot amendment.

Next steps we propose:
- You share a 30/90-day traffic profile (rough counts and peak windows).
- We agree pilot length and visibility (alerts/tracing) and get a DocuSign for the pilot amendment.

I can jump on a 30-min call tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Commercial Partnerships, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_sla_template_v2.pdf)

Subject: Fwd: SLA request: 99.95 uptime + monthly credit cap adjustment

Team —

Forwarding Claire's redlines. Quick read: Skyforge is asking for 99.95 and a 60% monthly cap for ramp. They want an answer quickly (EOD Mon 7/19). Recommendations? My thinking: Option A as a timeboxed pilot reduces long-term exposure and helps close the deal — we get to observe real traffic while giving them higher upfront assurance. Need to confirm with Legal that the 60% pilot cap is acceptable with the 2x per-incident limiter (protects us on catastrophic pricing). Also want CS to own the instrumentation/alerts requirement.

Laura — your call on whether Commercial signs the pilot amendment. Marissa — can Legal turn around a pilot amendment this week with the limit language and an acceptance clause tied to usage? If we cannot land Option A, Option B is an alternative but may require stronger definition of "critical outage" to avoid ambiguous triggers.

Thanks —
Aditya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Claire Morton <claire@skyforge.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA request: 99.95 uptime + monthly credit cap adjustment

Claire —

Thanks for the patience. We discussed internally and can offer the following compromise to expedite procurement approval while managing enterprise risk: 

- Pilot amendment (6 months): Redwood will commit to 99.95% monthly uptime for Skyforge for the first 6 months following go-live.
- During the pilot period only, the monthly credit cap for remedies triggered by availability breaches will be increased to a maximum of 60% of the monthly invoice. 
- Credit mechanics: per-incident remedy stays on the standard ladder (percent of monthly invoice by downtime band). We will apply a per-incident multiplier that does not exceed 2x for cumulative exposure calculation to prevent compounding beyond the 60% cap.
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance (48h notice), customer misconfiguration, and force majeure remain excluded. For batched inference latency deviations we will set endpoint-level P95 targets after we review your 30/90-day traffic profile.

Action items for Skyforge to finalize terms quickly:
1) Sign the pilot amendment via DocuSign (link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/SF-SLA-1147) — I'll send the DocuSign today with tracked language.
2) Share a 30-day and 90-day traffic sample (CSV or shared Drive link).
3) Confirm go-live window so we can align maintenance blackout periods during ramp.

If you prefer the non-pilot path (long-term 99.95) we can discuss additional commercial guardrails but that will require a separate underwrite. The pilot route is the fastest path to get you the higher uptime floor and close the quarter.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: final_pilot_amendment_redlines.pdf)
